messages:
Ravi N: Heads up — ran into a weird flow while setting up a demo VM. installer said install complete but `redwoodctl login` immediately errors with TLS when profile endpoint is internal.
Clara: paste error?
Ravi N: `Error: POST "https://auth.internal.redwood.svc/oauth/device": x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`
Marta S: that sounds like the installer merged an internal endpoint during discovery fallback. Did the installer print a discovery warning?
Ravi N: it did: 'Discovery failed; using cached control plane https://auth.internal.redwood.svc' — made sense at the time for CI images but not for a laptop.
Clara: quick fix: edit `~/.redwood/config.yaml` and set profile.endpoint to `https://auth.redwood.ai`, then run `REDWOODCTL_FORCE_PUBLIC=1 redwoodctl login --profile demo --method device`
Ravi N: that worked. FWIW, we also needed `redwoodctl local-serve --profile demo --trust-ca /tmp/corp-ca.pem` for the local dev server to accept the corp CA. saved me from installing CA system-wide.
Kai L: thanks — two follow-ups: 1) installer should default to public endpoints for interactive installs and ask before preserving cached internal endpoints, and 2) CLI should emit a one-liner hint when login fails due to certs with the suggested fixes (force env / trust-ca) so workshop attendees have an action.
Marta S: PR idea: change interactive installer flow to prefer public endpoints unless `--preserve-internal` is passed. Also add telemetry note when cached endpoints are used.
DevEx Bot: created DEVEX-1740 "installer: avoid silently merging cached internal endpoints for interactive installs; surface clear remediation hints on CLI auth failures" (priority=P2)
Clara: also noticed the CLI auth retry/backoff is shorter than SDKs — testers saw flaky failures during slow network. we should align retry behavior between tools. filing a follow-up.
Ravi N: opened a small onboarding doc edit to include `--trust-ca` and `REDWOODCTL_FORCE_PUBLIC` examples for offline/demo setups. Will update once PR lands. Thanks all :thumbsup:
